title: Missing cell clears the validity flag
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $d:\mathbb{N}\to\mathrm{Option}({\mathrm{CellV}(N)})$, and let $m\in\mathbb{N}$. If $d(j)$ is absent for some $j<m$, then after folding the option-valued cell update over $d(0),\ldots,d(m-1)$ from the initial validation state, the first validity flag is false.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols
